name: Workbench P-005 Windows resident lifecycle and harness audit
summary: The maintained signed-in Windows resident lifecycle passed45 assertions with current Organizer source. This current-build fixture proof does not establish installed-artifact three-OS acceptance or shipment.

audit.rootCause: The native lifecycle wrapper used the generic35s deadline for a sequence of seven individually bounded controller operations plus settings waits. It terminated a progressing fixture at Enable, outside any controller failure. The direct SSH caller in v1 separately violated the interactive-desktop precondition; production correctly refused it.
audit.durableFix: One declared controller sequence now supplies the lifecycle wrapper and Node client deadline contract. Existing12s per-controller and5s UI-wait bounds are unchanged. Sequence changes fail before dispatch unless the contract matches. Bare Resident preflights its window station before creating state; failed children retain budgets/progress/logs and remove only their exact newly-created controller registration. Nested diagnostics similarly compose both child budgets and emit phase progress.
audit.distinguishingTest: Use identical native production source hashes on the signed-in desktop with the maintained lifecycle fixture, whose parent contract contains the complete controller sequence without widening any child deadline.
audit.actualObservation: All45 lifecycle checks passed, including Install, no-op reinstall, Settings save-disable, disabled Run, Enable, Disable and Uninstall. Separate19 diagnostics passed, including hard-kill cleanup and4registration preservation/removal controls.
audit.unresolved: An earlier diagnostics control SSH launch timed out65s with no output. Subsequent exact process/task read found none and no new retained directory; its cause is unknown. Final diagnostics has explicit remote startup/result/exit receipts and19passes; no earlier pass is inferred.
